newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israelis wound three Arabs in Hebron clashes.
newsitem.headline: Israelis wound three Arabs in Hebron clashes.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded three Palestinians on Thursday in fresh clashes with Arab stone-throwers in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.

Israel's defence minister, meanwhile, told troops the Jewish state could easily recapture West Bank towns handed over to the PLO under self-rule deals but preferred that the Palestinian Authority curb the violence.

"There would be no difficulty recapturing Hebron or any other city but we don't want to do that," Yithzak Mordechai told soldiers in northern Israel. "We want the Palestinians to honour the agreements."

Palestinians in Hebron said about 200 Arabs, including many children, gathered at Shallaleh street which divides Hebron into Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled areas and hurled stones and petrol bombs at Israeli soldiers.
They said soldiers responded with rubber-coated metal bullets. Officials at the government-run Alia hospital said three Palestinians were treated for rubber bullet injuries and sent home.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said three petrol bombs were thrown at troops. She knew of no Palestinian casualties.
Witnesses said a large Palestinian police force arrived to disperse protesters.

Israeli soldiers shot dead two Palestinians on Tuesday and wounded more than 100 during clashes that followed the killing of a shopkeeper by two Jewish settlers. The settlers said they were attacked by Palestinians, Arab witnesses said the shooting was unprovoked.
Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 has sparked almost daily Palestinian protests and clashes with Israeli security forces.
Palestinians said the Israeli army imposed a curfew on the West Bank village of Surif and detained five Palestinians, including the director of a private hospital in Hebron.
